message: Can you read this ECG for me?
reply:
My preliminary reading is **sinus rhythm at about 60–65 beats/minute, with mild variation in the heart rate**.

- The electrical axis and conduction intervals appear normal.
- There are prominent chest-lead voltages, with mild upward-curving ST elevation and upright T waves in V2–V4.
- This could represent a **normal repolarization variant**, often called early repolarization. I don’t see obvious reciprocal ST depression or pathological Q waves.

**The image alone cannot confirm that these changes are benign.** Symptoms and comparison with an older ECG are important when assessing ST elevation. [Clinical reference](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2008.12.014)

If you have current chest pain, shortness of breath, sweating, or fainting, seek emergency care now.

How old are you, why was the ECG taken, and were you having any symptoms?
